title: AI literacy in K-12: a systematic literature review
extended_summary:
This paper asks how artificial intelligence (AI) literacy is being integrated into K-12 education worldwide. The authors conduct a systematic literature review to map the field, identify major approaches, and highlight gaps in current research and implementation. They review 179 documents retrieved from Scopus using a search strategy centered on AI literacy/education and school levels, while excluding papers focused only on computer-based learning or intelligent tutoring systems.

The review organizes the literature into two broad categories: learning experiences and theoretical perspectives. Learning experiences include activities aimed at helping K-12 students recognize AI in artifacts, understand how AI works, use AI-related tools, and reflect on the societal and ethical implications of AI. Theoretical perspectives include curriculum design, AI as a subject, student perspectives, teacher training, support resources, and gender diversity. The paper notes that many learning experiences emphasize technical or applied skills but rarely assess student learning outcomes rigorously.

The authors conclude that AI literacy in K-12 should be interdisciplinary, competency-based, and integrated into existing subjects rather than added as a standalone course. They argue that curricula should be modular, contextualized, and co-designed with teachers, and that teacher preparation is essential for successful implementation. The review also emphasizes the importance of ethics, social implications, and critical engagement with AI, while noting that current work is still limited and uneven across countries.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed systematic literature review, but it synthesizes heterogeneous K-12 AI literacy papers rather than reporting a causal evaluation of a single intervention. The methodology is transparent and structured, yet the evidence base is largely descriptive and the paper does not provide pooled effect estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: The review identifies important implementation directions for K-12 AI literacy, including curriculum design, teacher co-design, and interdisciplinary integration, but it does not demonstrate measured student outcome impacts. Its practical value is moderate and mainly strategic rather than evidentiary for achievement effects.
